Colville

This starting guide follows cultural-preservation work published by the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation. Its history and archaeology program and its language division offer complementary entry points into records, Elders’ accounts and learning resources. These institutional introductions are not a complete history of the distinct peoples represented within the confederation.

03

A tribal institution for historical research

The History/Archaeology Program describes work across archaeology, ethnography, history and cultural-resource management on the Columbia Plateau. Its public services include archival research, oral-history review and transcription, traditional-skills research, collections management and museum interpretation. The page explains how an institution approaches evidence and preservation; it does not itself supply the linked films’ full content or the separate histories of every constituent people.

Read the sources [1] Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation

04

Language work across generations

The Cultural Preservation Division describes a responsibility to preserve and share language, culture and history with coming generations. Its account emphasizes recording and carefully preserving Elders’ stories, and supporting dictionaries, curriculum, translation and access to fluent speakers. Read these as the division’s responsibilities and educational routes. The directory has not assessed the linked lessons, recordings or language outcomes, and restricted community knowledge is not made public by a program listing.

Read the sources [4] Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, Cultural Preservation Division

About Us — Colville Tribes Language Program ↗

The complete short explanatory body describes preserving Elders’ accounts, supporting language learning and passing culture and history to coming generations. Its stated aims and provision of dictionaries and curriculum are not a measurement of language proficiency or program success.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual Colville Language body, reader lines 296–305: Cultural Preservation Division mandate, recording and preserving Elders’ stories, educational media, three language programs, dictionary/curriculum/translation services. Linked recordings, dictionaries, classes and certification forms not reviewed.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026
